label: Excellent
corporate_parent: BSH Home Appliances Corporation — subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH
manufacturing_location: BSH production facilities (E.G.O. coils, Infineon IGBTs, Schott CERAN glass)

induction_system.description: 48 individual 3-inch inductor elements (newer models: 56 elements). Proprietary software maps size, shape, and position of cookware placed anywhere on the surface. Eliminates fixed cooking zones — the defining innovation in residential induction.
induction_system.effective_cooking_area: 63% more effective cooking area than fixed-zone competitors
induction_system.power_board: Multi-channel inverter architecture (estimated 8-16 independent channels) required to drive 48+ elements. Fundamentally more complex electronics than 4-channel fixed-zone systems.

coil_supplier.notes: Array of small independent elements using E.G.O. coil assemblies

igbt_supplier.notes: HighSpeed3 H3 series IGBTs for power switching

glass_ceramic.grade: CERAN grade — specific Miradur confirmation not available

interface.description: 6.5-inch full-color TFT touchscreen for all controls. Pan-mapping visualization and settings.
interface.documented_issues: Laggy performance, unresponsiveness with grease/water splatter, occasional system freezes requiring breaker reset. This is the most significant UX pain point.

performance_evidence.watts_detail: 4600W per zone — boost mode, likely temporary (10-20 min estimated)
performance_evidence.boil_time: excellent — sub-2 minute boil documented for PowerBoost mode
performance_evidence.pan_placement: Full-surface flexibility — cookware anywhere on glass. Accommodates rectangular griddles, multiple pots simultaneously.
performance_evidence.cooking_area_advantage: 63% more vs fixed-zone — genuine performance differentiator

yale_service_rate.context: Thermador induction 4.9% vs Bosch induction 1.7%. Hypothesis: Freedom's complex multi-channel electronics explain the ~3x gap. More elements = more failure points.

common_failures.power_board_inverter: Service calls frequently involve power board/inverter issues. Multi-channel architecture is expensive to repair ($400-$800+ estimated for power board replacement).
common_failures.pan_detection: Errant pan-detection errors and 'no pan' false-positives documented.
common_failures.thermal_shutdown: Cooling fan failures can trigger thermal shutdown — cascading failure risk.
common_failures.touchscreen: Moisture/condensation under glass can trigger error codes or erratic behavior.

service_network.description: BSH factory-trained or specialized technicians required. Parts are proprietary to BSH/Thermador platform. Repair costs significantly higher than standard consumer-grade cooktops.

parts_availability.description: BSH parts available through authorized distributors. Power board modules are expensive.

control_board.notes: Complex multi-channel power electronics with documented early-model reliability issues. Improving in newer production runs.

safety_evidence.recalls: None identified for Thermador Freedom Induction
safety_evidence.emc: FCC Part 18 compliant — induction generates RF from 20-100 kHz coils

platform_disclosure.bsh_shared_platform: MANDATORY: Thermador shares BSH induction platform core electronics (E.G.O. coils, Infineon IGBTs, Schott CERAN glass) with Bosch and Gaggenau. However: Freedom full-surface hardware (48-56 element array, multi-channel inverter, pan-mapping software) is genuinely unique to Thermador — NOT a rebadged Bosch.
platform_disclosure.freedom_vs_bosch_differentiation: Freedom uses 8-16 independent inverter channels vs Bosch's ~4 channels. Freedom's 48+ element coil array is fundamentally different from Bosch FlexInduction's dual-zone bridging. This explains the 4.9% vs 1.7% service rate gap — complexity premium.

corrections.reason: Deep dive found newer Freedom models use 56 elements
